- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check check-all-engines clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

verify-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/verify $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

1	# andesim-demo
2	
3	Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
4	every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
5	(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
10	  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
11	- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).
12	
13	## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`
14	
15	Fill in these settings if your paths differ:
16	
17	```Makefile
18	ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
19	TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
20	ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
21	```
22	
23	## Step 2: Build
24	
25	```bash
26	make
27	```
28	
29	Each demo links against the andesim runtime
30	(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
31	runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.
32	
33	## Step 3: Run
34	
35	Run every mode of one demo:
36	
37	```bash
38	make run-hello
39	make run-lm
40	make run-lm_slave
41	make run-lm_dma
42	make run-hvm_slave
43	make run-hvm_dma
44	make run-rvv
45	make run-fp
46	make run-cache
47	make run-verify
48	make run-syscall
49	make run-coremark
50	make run-dhrystone
51	```
52	
53	Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
54	`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `verify-*`,
55	`syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):
56	
57	| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
58	|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
59	| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
60	| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |

100	  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
101	  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

104	each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of

115	vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU

236	| lm_dma    | PASS | PASS | - |

238	| hvm_dma   | PASS | PASS | - |
239	| rvv       | PASS | PASS | - |

241	| cache     | PASS | PASS | - |
242	| verify    | PASS | PASS | - |
243	| syscall   | PASS | PASS | - |

277	demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff

287	demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
288	demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
289	```

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-cache
make run-verify
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |

name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: "vsim:ax66_makatau fails HTIF syscalls (gettimeofday, file io) in --mode cycle; TWO plausible theories built from static/vendor docs both disproven by runtime facts; root cause still open"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
---

`make check-all-engines` (in andesim-demo) sweeps all 3 vsim engines
(`ax45mpv_premium`, `ax46mpv_advanced`, `ax66_makatau`) and found
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first-ever HTIF syscall, `gettimeofday()`, fails right after boot. The
other two engines and `--mode fast` (QEMU) pass fine.

**Bisection evidence (empirical, still valid, from running real ELFs on
sim_ax66_makatau):**
- `vplat_hello.elf` (UART printf only, no HTIF) - PASSES.
- `vplat_exit41.elf` (SimControl exit only, no HTIF) - PASSES.
- `vplat_gettimeofday.c` / `vplat_file.elf` (both use the HTIF
  magicmem mechanism) - FAIL. `vplat_file.elf` fails harder: a
  SystemC/TLM "target socket not found for address 0x6300050980"
  (~424GB, nonsense) + CPU trap (mcause 0x2).
- The SAME compiled ELF runs against all 3 engines (test loops
  `for eng in ax45mpv_premium ax46mpv_advanced ax66_makatau`) - this is
  `andesim`'s deliberate "engine-blind" design (see
  `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`'s header comment). Any theory that
  requires ax66 to see a DIFFERENT guest address than the other two
  engines for the SAME ELF is very likely wrong - check symbol
  addresses (`nm`) before trusting it.

**THEORY 1, DISPROVEN (session 1).** Suspected `flush_dcache()`'s L2
MMIO writeback (`mmsc_cfg` bit 46 gate) in `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
Disproven by bisection: skipping that whole code block, ax66 still
fails identically. See git history / old revisions of this note for
detail if needed - not repeating here, it's a dead end.

**THEORY 2, DISPROVEN (session 2 - this one).** Found (by reading
`vsim_andesim`'s source directly) that `ax66_makatau` supports an
"alias region" onto main RAM: `RAM_ALIAS_BASE = 0x800000000` in
`src/platform/memory_map.h`, registered unconditionally for all engines
in `Platform`'s constructor (`src/platform/platform.hpp:71`). Found that
`SimControl::dispatch()` (`src/platform/sim_control.hpp`) and
`guest_va_to_host()` (`src/htif/sys_call.hpp`) both resolved a guest
pointer as `addr - region.base_address`, NEVER checking
`alias_region` - a real bug, confirmed by writing a passing/failing
unit test (`src/tests/platform/sim_control.test.cpp`, still in the repo,
still green) and fixed via a new `SimpleMemory::base_for(addr)` helper
(picks `alias_region.base_address` vs `region.base_address` by
containment). Also fixed a genuinely separate, pre-existing bug found
along the way: `src/htif/command.hpp` was missing `#include <cstdint>`
(fixed, structural, zero behavior change).

**This fix is REAL but WRONG FOR THIS BUG - IT DOES NOT FIX THE
OBSERVED FAILURE.** Confirmed by rebuilding the actual `sim_ax66_makatau`
binary (via the repo's proper containerized build, see "How to build"
below) with the fix applied, and re-running
`andesim/tests/vplat/test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh`: **identical failure,
byte for byte** (`GETTIMEOFDAY: call failed`).

Root of the mistake: `RAM_ALIAS_BASE=0x800000000` matches
`DDR3_MEM_BASE` in the AX66 **vendor's own sample test patterns**
(`external/ax66/andes_vip/patterns/samples/include/platform.h`) - a
SEPARATE, vendor-authored test harness, unrelated to `andesim`'s guest
runtime. Checked (via `nm`) where `andesim`'s ACTUAL compiled test
ELFs place `magicmem`: `vplat_gettimeofday.elf` -> `0x108e80`,
`vplat_file.elf` -> `0x109a80` - both low addresses, near the `0x100000`
entry point, controlled by `andesim/runtime/andesim.ld`, the SAME for
all 3 engines (confirms the "engine-blind" note above). These addresses
are nowhere near the `0x800000000` alias window, so `base_for()`
resolves them via the plain `region` path regardless of the fix -
**the fix is a no-op for this specific bug.** The alias-region gap is
still a real, independently-confirmed bug (kept fixed, unit-tested,
worth keeping) - it just isn't THIS bug.

**Lesson (this is now TWO theories in a row disproven by not checking
real runtime values first):** a vendor datasheet or a "looks similar"
constant/config from a DIFFERENT test harness in the same repo can be
completely inapplicable to the actual code path being debugged, even
when it's real, correctly-read, and internally consistent. Before
trusting ANY address/constant/config value as relevant: check what the
ACTUAL failing ELF/binary really uses at runtime (`nm`, `readelf`,
actual build's `config.inc`, actual linker script) - do this FIRST,
before forming a theory from docs/vendor samples/other-engine
templates, not after.

**Root cause: still OPEN.** What's actually confirmed and still true:
- The bug is specific to the HTIF magicmem mechanism (not UART, not
  the plain SimControl exit signal).
- It is NOT the L2/L3 cache MMIO flush code (theory 1, disproven).
- It is NOT an alias-region/guest-address-translation issue for THIS
  ELF (theory 2, disproven) - the addresses involved are plain, low,
  identical across all 3 engines.
- `vplat_file.elf`'s crash address (`0x6300050980`, ~424GB) is a THIRD
  number, matching neither the low guest addresses nor the alias base -
  unexplained. Possibly pointer corruption somewhere else, or an
  ax66-specific (mk_core family, first S/U-mode-capable engine, has an
  MMU/PMA/PMP per the datasheet - unlike the M-mode-only kv_core family
  ax45/ax46) address-translation/PMA/PMP default-state difference that
  affects even identity-mapped low addresses. NOT YET INVESTIGATED -
  this is the next lead, not a conclusion.

**How to build vsim_andesim (learned this session, wasted real time
before finding it):** do NOT try to build natively by hand-patching
CMakeCache.txt paths etc - this repo's build was made INSIDE a pinned
Docker/Podman container (see `Dockerfile`), and native builds hit
unrelated, pre-existing dependency breakage (e.g. vendored `LIEF`
missing `#include <cstdint>`, vendored `systemc-components` API
mismatch) with newer host compilers. Use `./build_vsim.sh` (builds the
`env` container image, runs `./build.sh` inside it with the repo
bind-mounted at `/work` - this is WHY `build/`'s CMakeCache.txt files
show `/work` paths; that's correct for this workflow, not stale. Only
hand-patch those paths if deliberately doing a native, non-Docker build
AND accepting the vendored-dependency risk). A full rebuild of all 4
CPUs takes appreciable time (single-CPU Verilation alone: ~7.5 min) -
budget for it, run in background, don't block on it synchronously.

**How to apply:** if asked to continue, do NOT restate either
disproven theory as fact. Next step should start from real ground
truth: dump/compare actual CSR state (mmsc_cfg, satp/PMA/PMP-related
CSRs if any) between a passing engine and ax66_makatau at the point
`htif_syscall()` executes, or trace exactly what address the CPU
actually puts on the bus for the magicmem write on ax66 vs the other
two (e.g. via vsim's own trace/debug logging) - don't theorize from
static docs again before doing this. User has been told twice now that
this investigation is open-ended and harder than scoped; check with
them before spending significant further effort.

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check check-all-engines clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

verify-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/verify $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

# ---- Shared configuration (can be overridden) ----

# Path to your andesim checkout, already built with scripts/build_all.sh.
ANDESIM ?= /home/nick/work/andesim

# Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `andesim doctor` reports).
XLEN ?= 64
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?= /local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d/bin/riscv$(XLEN)-unknown-elf-

COPILOT ?= 

# Cycle-accurate engine for --mode cycle / hybrid.
# See `andesim list engines` for what is available.
ENGINE ?= vsim:ax45mpv_premium

# Compiler optimization flag
OPT_LEVEL ?= -O2

# Extra flags for every andesim invocation, e.g. --log-level 1
ANDESIM_FLAGS ?=

# ---- Do not touch the followings ----

ANDESIM_BIN := $(ANDESIM)/andesim
RUNTIME := $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

          -B $(RUNTIME) -specs=andesim.specs

# gettimeofday() must succeed on every vsim engine, not just the default.
# ax66_makatau's mmsc_cfg reports PL2C (L2 cache) support even though its
# build has zero L2 KB configured; vplat_syscalls.c's flush_dcache(), run
# before every HTIF syscall, must not treat that as "safe to touch the L2
# MMIO window" -- gettimeofday is the runtime's first syscall, so a bad
# probe there fails before the ROI even starts.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_gettimeofday.elf"
QEMU="${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh): $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_gettimeofday.elf >/dev/null \
  || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local out rc
  out=$(timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'gettimeofday ok' \
    || fail "$label: missing 'gettimeofday ok': $out"
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0 (output: $out)"

/*
 * Copyright (c) 2017 Andes Technology Corporation
 * All rights reserved.
 *
 * This file defines the reset/nmi/trap handlers, the reset initialization code
 * and the trap entry table for Vectored-PLIC.
 *
 * Please note that the code in this file is to facilitate AndesCore processor
 * verification and it is NOT a goal for this code to be used in production.
 * For sample production version of start.S, please find it in Andes Startup
 * demos.
 */

#include "core_v5.h"

	.section .text
	.align 6

.global m_trap_entry
m_trap_entry:
	addi sp, sp, -40*REGBYTES

	/* Save caller registers */
	STORE x0, 0*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x1, 1*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x3, 3*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x4, 4*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x5, 5*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x6, 6*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x7, 7*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x8, 8*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x9, 9*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x10, 10*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x11, 11*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x12, 12*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x13, 13*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x14, 14*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x15, 15*REGBYTES(sp)
#ifndef __riscv_32e
	STORE x16, 16*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x17, 17*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x18, 18*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x19, 19*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x20, 20*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x21, 21*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x22, 22*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x23, 23*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x24, 24*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x25, 25*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x26, 26*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x27, 27*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x28, 28*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x29, 29*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x30, 30*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE x31, 31*REGBYTES(sp)
#endif

	/* Save mstatus and mepc */
	csrr t0, mepc
	csrr t1, mstatus
	csrr t2, mxstatus

	STORE t0, 32*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE t1, 33*REGBYTES(sp)
	STORE t2, 34*REGBYTES(sp)

	/* Call trap handler */
	csrr a0, mcause
	mv   a1, sp
	call handle_trap

	/* Disable interrupt */
	csrrci a5, mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE

	/* Restore mstatus and mepc */
	LOAD t0, 32*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD t1, 33*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD t2, 34*REGBYTES(sp)

	csrw mepc, t0
	csrw mstatus, t1
	csrw mxstatus, t2

	/* Restore caller registers */
	LOAD x0, 0*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x1, 1*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x3, 3*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x4, 4*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x5, 5*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x6, 6*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x7, 7*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x8, 8*REGBYTES(sp)

	LOAD x11, 11*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x12, 12*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x13, 13*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x14, 14*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x15, 15*REGBYTES(sp)
#ifndef __riscv_32e
	LOAD x16, 16*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x17, 17*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x18, 18*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x19, 19*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x20, 20*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x21, 21*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x22, 22*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x23, 23*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x24, 24*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x25, 25*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x26, 26*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x27, 27*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x28, 28*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x29, 29*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x30, 30*REGBYTES(sp)
	LOAD x31, 31*REGBYTES(sp)
#endif

	addi sp, sp, 40*REGBYTES
	mret

#=========================================================================
# crt0.S : Entry point for RISC-V user programs
#=========================================================================

#ifndef CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
#define CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS 0
#endif

#define mcache_ctl 0x7ca
#define mmisc_ctl 0x7d0

  .text
  .global _start
  .type   _start, @function
_start:
  # Enable icache
  csrsi   mcache_ctl, 0x1

#ifdef ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE
  # Enable dcache coherence management
  li      a0, 1 << 19
  csrs    mcache_ctl, a0
1:
  csrr    a0, mcache_ctl
#if __nds_v5
  bbc     a0, 20, 1b
#else
  srli    a1, a0, 20
  andi    a1, a1, 1
  beqz    a1, 1b
#endif
#endif

  # Enable d-cache and hardware prefetch
  ori     a0, a0, 0x703
  csrw    mcache_ctl, a0

  .weak   _stack
  # Initialize stack pointer (if defined)
  lla     a0, _stack
  beqz    a0, 1f
  mv      sp, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  slli    a0, a0, 12
  sub     sp, sp, a0
#endif

  # Initialize global pointer
.option push
.option norelax
1:lla gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop

#ifdef __nds_v5
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg
  bbc     a0, 3, 1f
  la      a1, _ITB_BASE_
  csrrw   x0, uitb, a1
1:
#if __riscv_xlen >= 64
  bbc     a0, 52, 1f
#else
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg2
  bbc     a0, 20, 1f
#endif
  csrr    a0, mrvarch_cfg
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  la      a0, __jvt_base$
  csrw    jvt, a0
#endif
1:

  # Set mstatus.fs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 13)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Set mstatus.vs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 10)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Enable unaligned memory access (mmisc_ctl.UNA)
  li      a0, (1 << 6)
  csrs    mmisc_ctl, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss

  li      a1, 0xa55a
.Lother_hart_wait_loop:
  ld      a0, other_hart_boot_flag
  bne     a0, a1, .Lother_hart_wait_loop
  j       .Lmain
#else
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss
  li      a0, 0x01234571
  li      a1, 0xe0080000
  sw      a0, 0(a1)
1:
  j       1b
#endif

  # Clear the bss segment
.Lclear_bss:
  la      a0, _edata
  la      a2, _end
  sub     a2, a2, a0
  li      a1, 0
  call    memset


#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  li      a0, 0xa55a
  lla     a1, other_hart_boot_flag
  sd      a0, 0(a1)
  fence
#endif

  call init_mtvec

.Lmain:
  li      a0, 0
  li      a1, 0
  li      a2, 0
  call    main

  call    _exit

.Lloop:
  j       .Lloop

  .size   _start, .-_start

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  .data
  .p2align 3
  .global other_hart_boot_flag
  .type   other_hart_boot_flag, @object
other_hart_boot_flag:
  .8byte 0
  .size other_hart_boot_flag, . - other_hart_boot_flag
#endif

What I have so far, from a direct on-silicon probe (`cctl_probe.elf` on `sim_ax66_makatau` vs `sim_ax45mpv_premium`):

Two mechanisms still fit (lingering clean L2 copy vs HW-prefetch refill of the stale line). They converge on the same fix family but I want to know which. Running the discriminator now, plus checking whether an uncacheable path exists for the proper fix.

input.content:
---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: "vsim:ax66_makatau fails HTIF syscalls in --mode cycle; ROOT CAUSE FOUND - host services syscalls by a backdoor write into the flat backing store, invisible to the guest through ax66's private write-back L2 (PL2C). Fix belongs in the vsim platform, not the guest runtime."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
---

`make check-all-engines` (andesim-demo) sweeps the rv64 vsim engines and
`vsim:ax66_makatau` fails `demo/syscall` in `--mode cycle`: the guest's
first HTIF syscall (`gettimeofday`) fails right after boot. ax45mpv_premium,
ax46mpv_advanced, and `--mode fast` (QEMU) all pass.

## ROOT CAUSE (found, evidence-backed - session 3)

The HTIF magicmem transport assumes host and guest share a coherent view of
RAM. They do not on ax66.

- The host services a syscall by writing the result **directly into the
  SystemC flat backing store** - `SimControl::dispatch()`
  (`vsim_andesim/src/platform/sim_control.hpp`) copies args from, and writes
  the return value back into, `data_region.data.begin() + offset`. That is a
  backdoor poke into `SimpleMemory::data` (`simple_memory.hpp`), which sits
  **behind** the Verilated core's caches. `SimpleMemory` only serves a read
  from `data` when the core actually issues a bus transaction; a line the
  core still holds is never refetched, so the host's write is invisible.
- On a core with a **private write-back L2**, the syscall buffers stay
  resident across the handoff and the guest reads its own stale copy. ax66
  has PL2C (256 KB; `mmsc_cfg` bit46 = 1, `mcache_ctl.pl2_en` bit32 = 1);
  ax45/ax46 have no PL2C (`NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB {0}`, bit46 = 0). That is the
  whole difference.

host has already written the result before the readback runs):**

| engine | PL2C | mmsc_cfg b46 | mcache_ctl | baseline read | tv_sec |
|--------|------|--------------|------------|---------------|--------|
| ax45mpv_premium | none | 0 | 1b03      | 0 (fresh) | real |
| ax46mpv_advanced| none | 0 | 1b03      | 0 (fresh) | real |
| ax66_makatau    | 256K | 1 | 100001f03 | 5 (stale) | 0 |

(gettimeofday's `tv`), not the dirty command word. ax66 reads the bss zero
(0), ax45/ax46 read the real timestamp. So this is genuinely host-write /
guest-cache incoherence, NOT the command word and NOT address translation.

- The architecturally correct move is "invalidate only the result buffers
  after the call." That needs **VA-scoped CCTL**, which **traps** on ax66:
  `mk_csr.v` sets `NO_CCTL_VA = RVH_SUPPORT`, and ax66 has
  `NDS_RVH_SUPPORT {yes}` -> VA-form CCTL commands are removed. (probe1:
  `L1D_VA_INVAL`/`L1D_VA_WBINVAL` -> traps=1 on ax66, =0 on ax45.)
- The "ALL" variants don't work: `L1D_WBINVAL_ALL` (cmd 6, what
  `vplat_syscalls.c::flush_dcache()` uses) leaves the guest reading stale;
  `L1D_INVAL_ALL` (cmd 23) would also drop unrelated dirty lines (stack) and
  corrupt the guest at a non-terminal point.
- No guest knob tested exposed the write: WBINVAL_ALL, INVAL_ALL,
  prefetch-off (clear IPREF/DPREF), and DC_COHEN all still read stale on
  ax66. (DC_COHEN can't help - the host poke bypasses the coherence bus.)

**Blocking layer = vsim platform** (per andesim-demo/CLAUDE.md taxonomy):
the SimControl/HTIF backdoor transport is incoherent with the modeled cache
hierarchy for private-write-back-L2 cores. NOT RTL-capability (ax66 has the
memory + CCTL), NOT the andesim driver, NOT the demo. Hybrid mode passes on
ax66 for hello/rvv/fp/etc. precisely because it drains **registers** via the
Debug Module (`state_drain.hpp`, DMI abstract reads) and never round-trips a
host write through guest RAM - so it never hits this.

## PROPER FIX (right layer = vsim, not yet implemented)

After `dispatch()` writes results into `data`, the simulator must make those
bytes visible to the core: invalidate the affected line(s) in the Verilated
core's L1/PL2C model, or issue the result write as a bus transaction the
caches observe - for every engine that models a write-back cache. The handler
already knows the guest addresses it wrote (magicmem, plus each syscall's
payload buffer: gettimeofday `tv`, read `buf`, stat `statbuf`, getcwd `buf`,
...). This is the coherence QEMU gets for free (no guest cache model).
Open question for implementation: whether the Verilated Andes model exposes a
cache-invalidate/flush backdoor, or one must be added. No such primitive
exists in the tree today (hybrid sidesteps RAM coherence via register drain).
Cheap guest-side confirmation not yet run: read the buffers through an
uncacheable mapping (e.g. the RAM_ALIAS 0x800000000 window if PMA marks it
NC) - should return fresh, proving the data is in `data` and only the cache
shadows it.

  fails identically. (That MMIO window is the kv-core shared-L2C mechanism;
  ax66's PL2C is private/CSR-controlled, so the block is a no-op there
  anyway.)

  low addresses (~0x109000), resolved via the plain `region` path; the

background, do not block synchronously. See [[vsim-build-via-container]].

-O2 -B /home/nick/work/andesim/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. Run:

after `. /home/nick/work/andesim/config.env` (exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN).

Root cause is settled - do not restate it as open or re-run the dead

content.text:
Root cause found. It is a cache-coherence bug in the vsim platform's syscall transport, triggered by one piece of hardware ax66 has and ax45/ax46 do not: a private write-back L2 cache (PL2C).

## What happens

The HTIF syscall path assumes the host and the guest see the same RAM. On ax66 they do not.

1. The guest runs `gettimeofday()`, which stages args in a `magicmem` buffer and pokes the HTIF command register (`vplat_syscalls.c`).
2. The host handler `SimControl::dispatch()` (`sim_control.hpp`) reads the args and writes the result **straight into the flat backing store** - `data_region.data.begin() + offset`. This is a backdoor poke into `SimpleMemory::data`, which sits *behind* the CPU's caches. A read is served from `data` only when the core actually puts a transaction on the bus.
3. ax66 has a private write-back L2 (PL2C, 256 KB). The syscall buffers stay cached across the handoff, so the guest reads its own stale copy - it never sees the host's write. ax45/ax46 have no PL2C, so their reads miss to the backing store and get the fresh value.

## Evidence (same ELF, three engines)

I wrote a probe that faithfully replays the `htif_syscall()` sequence then reads the result back:

| Engine | Private L2 | `mmsc_cfg` bit46 | Result read | `tv_sec` read |
|--------|-----------|------------------|-------------|---------------|
| ax45mpv_premium | none | 0 | 0 (fresh) | real time |
| ax46mpv_advanced | none | 0 | 0 (fresh) | real time |
| ax66_makatau | **256 KB PL2C** | **1** | **5 (stale)** | **0** |

The `tv_sec` column is the clincher: that is a plain host-written payload buffer, not the command word. ax66 reads back the bss zero; the others read the real timestamp. So this is host-write / guest-cache incoherence, plain - **not** the disproven theories (L2 MMIO flush, alias-address translation).

Why the guest runtime cannot just work around it on ax66: the correct move is "invalidate only the result buffer after the call," which needs VA-scoped CCTL - and ax66 **traps** on that, because it is hypervisor-capable (`NDS_RVH_SUPPORT=yes` sets `NO_CCTL_VA` in the RTL). The blunt "invalidate all" would corrupt unrelated dirty stack lines. Neither WBINVAL, INVAL-all, prefetch-off, nor DC_COHEN exposed the write in my tests.

## Blocking layer and fix

**Layer: vsim platform** (the SimControl/HTIF backdoor transport), not RTL capability, not the driver, not the demo. Hybrid mode passes on ax66 only because it drains **registers** via the Debug Module and never round-trips a host write through guest RAM.

**Proper fix (vsim-side):** after `dispatch()` writes the result into `data`, the simulator must make those bytes visible to the core - invalidate the affected line(s) in the Verilated cache model, or issue the write as a bus transaction the caches snoop - for any engine with a write-back cache. This is the coherence QEMU gets for free. Open implementation question: whether the Verilated Andes model exposes a cache-invalidate backdoor, or one must be added (nothing in the tree does this today).

I did **not** implement it - your ask was to find the root cause, and the fix is a vsim change plus a full container rebuild (~7.5 min/CPU). I updated the `ax66-makatau-syscall-bug` memory from "open" to "found" with the evidence.

(The stale wakeup above asked about the sweep + README - both were already finished last turn, nothing to redo there.)

Want me to implement the vsim fix? If so I'd start from the existing RED test (`test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh` fails on ax66), add a SimControl-level unit test, then make the syscall writeback cache-coherent.

Let me explain it simply, with a picture.

**The one-line version:** the ax66 program reads an old, cached value instead of the answer the simulator just wrote. So it thinks the syscall failed.

**The picture:**

Think of main memory as a **whiteboard** in a shared room.

- The program (the simulated CPU) is lazy. It keeps a **sticky note** copy of the whiteboard on its desk, so it does not have to walk to the room every time. This sticky note is the "cache."
- The program asks the simulator: "what time is it?"
- The simulator walks to the room and writes the time **on the whiteboard**.
- But the program does **not** look at the whiteboard again. It looks at its own **sticky note**, which still shows the OLD value.
- Result: the program reads the wrong answer and reports "syscall failed."

**Why only ax66 breaks:**

- ax45 and ax46 chips do **not** keep that extra sticky note. They always read the whiteboard directly, so they see the fresh time. They work.
- ax66 has an extra private cache (its "sticky note"). So it keeps reading the stale copy. It fails.

That is the whole bug. I proved it by running the same program on all three chips: only the one with the extra cache read the wrong value.

**Whose fault / where to fix:**

The simulator, when it writes the answer on the whiteboard, should also **throw away the program's sticky note** - force the program to re-read the fresh value. Right now it does not do that. So the fix goes in the **simulator code** (vsim), not in the chip and not in the demo.

Which part is confusing - the cache idea, or why it is the simulator's job to fix? I can go deeper on either one.

Two questions. Let me take the hybrid one first, because it clears up a mix-up.

**No, this is not hybrid.** The syscall fails in `--mode cycle` (pure cycle mode, no QEMU, no handoff). Hybrid is actually the one mode that does NOT hit this bug, because hybrid copies **registers** out of the CPU, not RAM. So "hybrid transport" is not involved. The problem is the **syscall data path** inside the plain vsim simulator.

**Now: why does the extra cache (PL2C) cause it?**

Back to the whiteboard picture. Let me add one thing.

- **Whiteboard** = the real memory (RAM).
- The simulator writes the answer **on the whiteboard directly**. It does not tell the program "hey, I changed it."

**ax45 / ax46 (no PL2C):**
- The program keeps **one** sticky note (the L1 cache).
- Before it asks for the answer, the program **throws its sticky note away** (this is `flush_dcache()` in the code).
- Now it has no copy. So to read, it **must walk to the whiteboard**. It sees the fresh answer. Works.

**ax66 (has PL2C):**
- The program keeps a sticky note (L1) **and** a folder in a drawer (the PL2C - a second, private cache).
- It throws the **sticky note** away. But the **folder in the drawer still has the old copy.**
- Now it reads. It checks the drawer first, finds the old copy there, and is happy. **It never walks to the whiteboard.**
- So it never sees the simulator's fresh answer. Fails.

That is the whole reason. PL2C is a **second place** where an old copy hides. The program's cleanup only clears the first place (L1), not the drawer (PL2C).

**Why does the program not just clear the drawer too?**
- The command to clear **just that one folder page** is turned off on ax66 (because ax66 is a bigger chip with hypervisor support; that feature disables the fine command - it traps).
- Clearing the **whole drawer** would also throw away other important notes it still needs (unsaved data on the stack). That would break the program.
- So the program **cannot** clean up safely. The simulator must do it instead.

So the fix: when the simulator writes on the whiteboard, it must also reach in and **clear the program's drawer** (invalidate the PL2C copy). Today it does not. That missing step is the bug, and it lives in the simulator (vsim), not the chip.

Does the "drawer" idea make it clearer? If yes, I can point to the exact lines in the code where the simulator writes to the whiteboard but skips clearing the drawer.

content.text:
`flush_dcache()` is in the runtime file that every demo links against:

**`/home/nick/work/andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`**

- Defined at `vplat_syscalls.c:72`
- Called at `vplat_syscalls.c:116`, inside `htif_syscall()`

The "throw away the sticky note" step is this one line inside it:

```c
// vplat_syscalls.c:72
static void flush_dcache(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));   // line 74  <-- clears L1 only
#if __riscv_xlen == 64
  ...L2 MMIO writeback block (0xe0500000)...                 // does NOT reach ax66's PL2C
#endif
}
```

And it is used here:

```c
// vplat_syscalls.c:105
static intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, ...)
{
  magicmem[0] = n;              // stage the args
  ...
  flush_dcache();               // line 116  <-- the cleanup
  *(volatile uint64_t*) HTIF_TOHOST_CMD = (uintptr_t) magicmem;  // line 117, ask the host
  __asm__ __volatile__("fence rw,rw" ::: "memory");
  return (intptr_t) magicmem[0];  // line 119  <-- reads back the answer (stale on ax66)
}
```

Line 74 is the key. `mcctlcommand = 6` means "L1D_WBINVAL_ALL" - clear the **L1** cache only (the sticky note). It never clears the **PL2C** (the drawer). The `#if` block below it tries to reach an L2 through a memory-mapped register at `0xe0500000`, but that is the mechanism for the **other** chip family (ax45's shared L2); ax66's PL2C is private and does not answer there. So on ax66 the drawer is never cleaned.

Note this line runs **before** asking the host (line 117), which is correct for sending the args. The missing step is a cleanup **after** line 117 and before the read on line 119 - and as I explained, the guest cannot do that cleanup safely on ax66, so the simulator has to.

content.text:
The problem is not gettimeofday itself. It is just the **first** message the program sends to the simulator. Any syscall would fail the same way. The inconsistency comes from how the message is passed: **two writers share one mailbox, but they use different paths.**

**The mailbox protocol.** The program and the simulator talk through a small memory buffer called `magicmem` (the "mailbox"):

1. Program writes the request into `magicmem`: "syscall number 5 = gettimeofday".
2. Program rings a doorbell (writes to a special address `0xe0080010`).
3. Simulator wakes up, reads the request from RAM, runs the real `gettimeofday()` on your PC, and writes the answer back into `magicmem[0]` (0 = success).
4. Program reads `magicmem[0]` to see the result.

**The key asymmetry.** The two sides do not access RAM the same way:

- The **program** (the simulated CPU) reads and writes **through its caches**, like real hardware.
- The **simulator** writes the answer **directly into the C++ array that models RAM**. It is like a ghost hand editing the RAM chip from outside. No bus signal. The caches are never told "this address changed".

A cache only updates when it sees traffic on the bus. A ghost write makes no traffic. So the cache keeps believing its old copy is correct.

**Timeline on ax66:**

```
program (CPU)                     RAM array              simulator
-------------                     ---------              ---------
magicmem[0] = 5  (into cache)
flush L1                 ------>  magicmem[0] = 5
   * PL2C keeps a copy: "5" *
ring doorbell            ----------------------------->  reads RAM: 5 = gettimeofday
                                                          runs gettimeofday()
                                  magicmem[0] = 0  <----  ghost-writes answer
                                                          (cache is NOT told)
read magicmem[0]:
  L1 miss (flushed) -> ask PL2C
  PL2C: "I have it! value = 5"    <-- never reaches RAM
gets 5, not 0  ->  "call failed"
```

The program expects 0 (success). It reads 5 (its own old request, still sitting in PL2C). 5 means failure, so it prints `GETTIMEOFDAY: call failed`.

**Why ax45/ax46 do not fail:** same timeline, but there is no PL2C level. After the L1 flush, **no cache** holds that line. The final read has nowhere to hit, so it must go to RAM - and RAM has the fresh answer 0. On ax66 the extra PL2C level still holds the line, because the program's flush command (`mcctlcommand=6`) cleans **L1 only**.

So: the data inconsistency = ghost write into RAM + one leftover cache copy in PL2C that nobody removes. ax66 is the only engine with that extra cache level, so it is the only one that fails.

On your earlier question ("can ax66 just flush PL2C?") - I checked the config while you asked: on ax66, the MMIO window at `0xe0500000` that the runtime's flush code pokes is the **L3 controller**, not PL2C, so that path cannot clean PL2C either. PL2C is controlled only through CCTL CSR commands, and my probe showed the useful forms either trap or do not expose the ghost write. That strengthens the conclusion: the guest cannot fix this; the simulator must invalidate the cache line (or write the answer through the bus) itself.

content.text:
There are two ways to fix it, at two different layers. Let me give you the picture first, then my recommendation.

## The design problem

Today the mailbox (`magicmem`) lives in **normal cacheable RAM**, and two masters that are **not coherent with each other** (the guest CPU with its caches, and the host with its ghost-hand backdoor) both read and write it. Any fix that keeps the mailbox in cacheable RAM has to fight the cache hierarchy of every engine, forever - ax66 today, the next core with an L3 tomorrow.

The clean fix: **move the mailbox out of RAM entirely, into the SimControl device itself.** Device space (`0xe008xxxx`) is already uncached on every engine - we know this empirically, because every UART byte and every doorbell write already reaches the device instantly, on all three engines. No cache can ever hold a copy of it.

```
today (broken on ax66):                 proposed:
guest -> cache -> RAM <- ghost host     guest -> uncached window in SimControl <- host
             ^ stale copies                      (no cache involved at all)
```

- Guest copies syscall args and payload into a small scratch window inside the SimControl region (e.g. `0xe0080800`, ~2KB), with plain uncached stores.
- Rings the doorbell. Host reads args **from its own device memory** - no RAM, no cache peek.
- Host writes results back into the window. Guest copies them out with uncached loads into its own buffers (its own cached writes are coherent with itself - no problem).
- Big `write()` buffers loop in 2KB chunks. Slow, but so is UART-per-character stdout, and this is a sim syscall layer.

Bonus: `flush_dcache()` can be **deleted completely** - including the fragile L2 MMIO block (which on ax66 pokes the L3 controller's address anyway, the wrong device). The whole class of bug disappears, engine-blind, for every future engine.

## Cost: it touches three components

| Component | Change |
|-----------|--------|
| `vsim_andesim/src/platform/sim_control.hpp` | add the scratch window + read args/write results from it; keep the old RAM-pointer path for old ELFs |
| QEMU mirror device (`andes_ae350.c`, the fork) | same window, same semantics - one ELF must still run on fast/cycle/hybrid |
| `andesim/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c` | rewrite `htif_syscall()` to marshal through the window; delete `flush_dcache()` |

Plus rebuilds: vsim platform (C++ only, no re-Verilation - fast, via `./build_vsim.sh`) and QEMU.

TDD path is ready-made: `test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh` is already RED on ax66; I would add SimControl unit tests for the window first, then make it green engine by engine.

## The cheaper alternative (vsim-only patch)

Keep the protocol; after `dispatch()` writes results into RAM, also reach into the **Verilated PL2C tag/data arrays** by backdoor and invalidate (or update) the matching lines. One repo, no QEMU rebuild. But: it is per-engine cache surgery (tag decode, set/way geometry), must be redone for every new cache level, and there is evidence the guest-to-host direction (args) is also flaky through PL2C - so the patch needs read-side surgery too. This is the "workaround" shape your CLAUDE.md tells me to avoid.

# Debug-Logging Roadmap: log levels -> reproducible bugs

Goal: use the `--log-level` scale (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error
5=critical 6=off, shared with vsim) so that any failed or suspicious run
can be REPRODUCED and diagnosed from its own output, without re-running
under ad-hoc printf debugging.

Principles
- info (default) stays clean: program output + the answer line. All new
  detail goes to debug/trace.
- errors always print, and every error should carry enough to reproduce.
- one scale end-to-end: andesim driver -> QEMU plugin -> vsim engine.
- input/output of every feature is a printable contract a test can grep.

Current state (done)
- driver/log.hpp/.cpp: threshold + log_on/log_line/log_result; --log-level
  and --log-file flags.
- info: `[andesim] N cycles`; debug: banner, mmap line, window mcycle
  detail, PASS, decision log; trace: exec command lines; warn:
  unsupported-CSR + mem-size notes.
- All of L0..L5 below are DONE (contract test:

# HTIF Syscall Window Roadmap: uncached mailbox, coherence by construction

Goal: `demo/syscall` (and all HTIF file io) passes on EVERY vsim engine,
including `vsim:ax66_makatau`, by removing the root cause found on
2026-07-14: the host services syscalls by backdoor-writing the flat RAM
model, which is invisible through a private write-back L2 (ax66's PL2C).
See memory note `ax66-makatau-syscall-bug` for the full evidence chain.

Fix: move the syscall mailbox OUT of cacheable RAM into a scratch window
inside the SimControl device region. Device space is uncached on every
engine (PMA device attribute - empirically proven by UART + doorbell
behavior on all 3 engines), so no cache can ever hold a stale copy, in
either direction. `flush_dcache()` becomes dead code and is deleted.

## The window contract (shared by vsim, QEMU, runtime)

- Region: SimControl `0xe0080000 - 0xe0080fff` (existing 4KB on both hosts).
- Window: offset `0x800..0xfff` (2KB), device-backed storage:
  - `0x800..0x83f`: eight u64 slots - syscall nr/args in, result in slot 0
    (same layout as the old RAM magicmem).
  - `0x840..0xfff`: 1984-byte data area for payload marshaling.
- Doorbell: offset `0x28` (`SYSCALL_GO`), u32/u64 write of any value ->
  host executes the syscall synchronously (b_transport), result visible
  in slot 0 on the very next guest load.
- Buffer-pointer convention: guest passes full guest VAs that point INTO
  the window data area (`0xe0080840+`); `guest_va_to_host()` resolves
  window VAs against the device storage, so all 17 syscall handlers stay
  unchanged.
- Guest access discipline: u64 loads/stores only (sd/ld) - matches the
  device-access sizes every engine already proves out via the 0x10 HTIF
  doorbell.
- Old protocol (RAM pointer via offset 0x10) stays intact for old ELFs.

## W1. vsim: extract run_syscall() (structural)

- Description: pull the syscall-table lookup + execute + writeback out of
  `SimControl::dispatch()` into `run_syscall(uint64_t args[8])`, so the
  old RAM path and the new window path share one execution core. No
  behavior change; existing unit tests stay green.
- Key files: vsim_andesim/src/platform/sim_control.hpp
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE

- Description: add the 2KB window storage + readable/writable window
  offsets + `SYSCALL_GO` doorbell to SimControl; `guest_va_to_host()`

  b_transport, ring 0x28, read result + tv payload back through the
  window), then GREEN.

Root-cause fix for the ax66 HTIF syscall failure: the legacy protocol
stages args/results in cacheable RAM (magicmem) which the host reads and
writes by BACKDOOR into the flat backing store -- invisible in either
direction through a private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C shadows the host's
result write; unit-provable stale readback). Coherence by construction
instead: a 2KB device-storage window in the upper half of the SimControl
region (offset 0x800: eight u64 arg/result slots + 1984B payload area,
doorbell SYSCALL_GO at 0x28, guest VAs into the window resolved by
guest_va_to_host's new window branch, all 17 handlers unchanged). Device
space is PMA-uncached on every engine, so no guest cache can ever hold a
copy. Legacy RAM-pointer protocol untouched for old ELFs.

Tests: window byte round-trip; full gettimeofday through the window with
backing RAM asserted untouched. 30/30 green.

QEMU mirror device + runtime switch land separately (one ELF must keep
running on fast/cycle/hybrid): see andesim ROADMAP_HTIF_WINDOW.md W4/W5.

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build QEMU out-of-tree under build/qemu/.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
BUILD="$SRC/build/qemu"

if [[ ! -x "$SRC/configure" ]]; then
  echo "missing $SRC/configure - run 'git submodule update --init --recursive'" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$BUILD"

if [[ ! -f "$BUILD/build.ninja" && ! -f "$BUILD/Makefile" ]]; then

1	# HTIF Syscall Window Roadmap: uncached mailbox, coherence by construction
2	
3	Goal: `demo/syscall` (and all HTIF file io) passes on EVERY vsim engine,
4	including `vsim:ax66_makatau`, by removing the root cause found on
5	2026-07-14: the host services syscalls by backdoor-writing the flat RAM
6	model, which is invisible through a private write-back L2 (ax66's PL2C).
7	See memory note `ax66-makatau-syscall-bug` for the full evidence chain.
8	
9	Fix: move the syscall mailbox OUT of cacheable RAM into a scratch window
10	inside the SimControl device region. Device space is uncached on every
11	engine (PMA device attribute - empirically proven by UART + doorbell
12	behavior on all 3 engines), so no cache can ever hold a stale copy, in
13	either direction. `flush_dcache()` becomes dead code and is deleted.
14	
15	## The window contract (shared by vsim, QEMU, runtime)
16	
17	- Region: SimControl `0xe0080000 - 0xe0080fff` (existing 4KB on both hosts).
18	- Window: offset `0x800..0xfff` (2KB), device-backed storage:
19	  - `0x800..0x83f`: eight u64 slots - syscall nr/args in, result in slot 0
20	    (same layout as the old RAM magicmem).
21	  - `0x840..0xfff`: 1984-byte data area for payload marshaling.
22	- Doorbell: offset `0x28` (`SYSCALL_GO`), u32/u64 write of any value ->
23	  host executes the syscall synchronously (b_transport), result visible
24	  in slot 0 on the very next guest load.
25	- Buffer-pointer convention: guest passes full guest VAs that point INTO
26	  the window data area (`0xe0080840+`); `guest_va_to_host()` resolves
27	  window VAs against the device storage, so all 17 syscall handlers stay
28	  unchanged.

---
name: ax66-makatau-syscall-bug
description: "ax66 HTIF syscall bug: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (2026-07-14) - host backdoor-wrote syscall results into flat RAM, invisible through ax66's private write-back PL2C; fixed by moving the mailbox into an uncached SimControl device window (vsim + QEMU + runtime, all committed)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2f3f544d-3989-4811-a594-f467b83e9ab4
---

`vsim:ax66_makatau` used to fail every HTIF syscall (`demo/syscall`,
gettimeofday, file io) in `--mode cycle`; ax45/ax46/QEMU passed.

## ROOT CAUSE (proven 2026-07-14)

The legacy HTIF protocol staged args/results in a `magicmem` block in
cacheable RAM; the host serviced calls by **backdoor** reads/writes of the
flat backing store (`SimpleMemory::data`), behind the Verilated core's
caches - no bus transaction, nothing snooped. Any core with a private
write-back L2 keeps serving its own stale copy. ax66 is the only engine
with one (PL2C 256KB, `mmsc_cfg` bit46=1); ax45/ax46 have none, so their
post-flush reads missed to RAM and got fresh data.

Controlled proof (same ELF, 3 engines, probe replaying `htif_syscall()`):
ax66 read back the staged syscall number (5) and `tv_sec=0`; ax45/ax46
read the result (0) and a real timestamp. The guest cannot fix it:
VA-scoped CCTL traps on ax66 (`NO_CCTL_VA = RVH_SUPPORT`, RVH=yes),
`*_ALL` invalidates drop unrelated dirty lines, and probes showed L1-only
ops are unreliable anyway (line migrates between L1 and PL2C).

## THE FIX (landed, all repos, TDD)

Mailbox moved OUT of RAM into device storage - coherence by construction
(device space is PMA-uncached on every engine). Contract in
`andesim/ROADMAP_HTIF_WINDOW.md`: 2KB window at SimControl +0x800 (eight
u64 arg/result slots + 1984B payload area), doorbell `SYSCALL_GO` at
+0x28, payload pointers are window VAs, guest uses u64 accesses only.
Legacy RAM protocol kept for old ELFs. `flush_dcache()` DELETED from the
runtime (its L2-MMIO block poked 0xe0500000, which on ax66 is the L3C
base - wrong device anyway).

Commits:
- vsim_andesim `c90c234` window + `8d71170` run_syscall extract
  (+ `b48cff5`/`5229426`: cstdint + alias-region fix, a separate real bug)
- qemu fork `2342ca8227` andes_ae350 sim_ctrl mirror
- andesim `0e3a13e` runtime rewrite + vplat_window fixture/test

Verified: `test_vplat_gettimeofday.sh` + `test_vplat_window.sh` green on
ax45/ax46/ax66 cycle + QEMU fast; vplat f1-f9/markers green;
`demo/syscall` SYSCALL_OK on ax66 in cycle and both hybrid triggers.

## Dead ends (do NOT re-open)
- Theory 1 (disproven): `flush_dcache()`'s L2C MMIO writeback path.
- Theory 2 (disproven for THIS bug): alias-region VA translation - real
  independent bug, fixed and unit-tested, but magicmem lived at low
  addresses so it was a no-op here.
- `vplat_file.elf`'s old wild-address crash (0x6300050980) was the same
  coherence hole in the guest->host direction: the host read stale args
  (a garbage buffer pointer) out of RAM the guest's caches still owned.

## Lesson (held)
Confirm from real runtime values, not docs/vendor samples: both dead
theories came from reading static config; the answer came from running
one ELF on all three engines and diffing behavior. When two masters
share memory through different paths (bus vs backdoor), suspect
coherence before address math.

## Build notes
vsim: `./build_vsim.sh` (container; native fails on vendored deps).
Platform-only C++ edits do NOT re-Verilate - incremental is minutes. Unit
tests build natively: `ninja -C build-utest test_sim_control && ctest`.
QEMU fork: `./build_qemu.sh` in qemu_andesim. Runtime/fixtures need
`. config.env` first (exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). See
[[vsim-build-via-container]].
